item.title: A Perturbative Two-Eigenvalue Faber-Krahn Problem for the Gaussian Short-Time Fourier Transform
item.description: arXiv:2611.33401v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that, for every fixed s\in (0,\infty), the set of area s maximizing the weighted sum of the first two eigenvalues of the associated Toeplitz operators on the Fock space must be a disc, up to translations and sets of measure zero. To do so, we first prove the existence of maximizer sets. Then we show that every maximizer set must be a perturbation of a disc when the weight is sufficiently small. Finally, we use the vector-valued version of the analytic implicit function theorem and the inverse function theorem to conclude that the perturbation must vanish when the weight tends to zero.
item.dc:creator: Yifan Zhang

item.title: The Kalton--Peck space disproves Rubio de Francia's conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.33556v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the classical complex Kalton--Peck space $Z_2$ is not isomorphic to $[X,H]_\theta$ for any UMD Banach space $X$, Hilbert space $H$, and $0<\theta<1$. Since $Z_2$ is UMD, this disproves Rubio de Francia's conjecture on intermediate UMD spaces. The proof combines the logarithmic block identity, a shift-commutator estimate on the interpolation strip, a unified obstruction in terms of reciprocal Hilbert norms, and Hahn--Banach with elementary convexity. It allows arbitrary compatible placements. We also realize $Z_2$ as a quotient of a closed subspace of an intermediate UMD space for every fixed interpolation parameter less than one.
item.dc:creator: Veli Shakhmurov, Rishad Shahmurov

item.title: Sharpness of the Kadec'-type theorem for the union of intervals
item.description: arXiv:2611.33606v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we establish the sharpness of a Kadec'-type theorem for finite unions of intervals admitting the integers as an orthonormal spectrum by constructing an explicit counterexample.
item.dc:creator: Thibaud Alemany, Oleg Asipchuk

item.title: Norm of the Generalized Hilbert Matrix Operator Between Some Spaces of Analytic Functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.33616v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the generalized Hilbert operator \[ \mathcal H_bf(z)=\int_0^1\frac{(1-t)^b}{(1-tz)^{b+1}}f(t)\,dt, \qquad b>0, \] on several spaces of analytic functions in the unit disk. For logarithmically weighted Korenblum spaces, we obtain an exact supremum representation and a lower estimate for the norm of the mapping from $H_{\alpha,\log}^{\infty}$ to $H_\alpha^\infty$. We then establish two-sided estimates and characterize the boundedness range of $\mathcal H_b$ on the $\alpha$-Bloch spaces $\mathcal B^\alpha$. We also derive norm bounds for the mapping from $H^\infty$ into the endpoint Zygmund-type space $\Lambda_1^{1,*}$. Furthermore, we give a norm representation for $\mathcal H_b:H_\alpha^\infty\to\mathcal B^{\alpha+1}$ and identify a norm-attaining function. In particular, for $0<\alpha\leq2/3$, the norm is expressed explicitly in terms of a Beta function. Finally, we obtain an exact supremum representation of the norm of $\mathcal H_b$ on $H_{\alpha,\log}^{\infty}$, together with explicit norm estimates. Our results extend those of Hao et al. [J. Geom. Anal. 35 (2025), Paper No. 184] for the classical Hilbert matrix operator ($b=0$) to the generalized case $b>0$.
item.dc:creator: Shaoyang Feng, Shanli Ye

item.title: A Non-Commutative Binomial Theorem, Extensions, and Applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.33774v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a matrix trace inequality analogous to the binomial theorem for reals: for Hermitian matrices $A$ and $B$, and a nonnegative even integer $k$ (and any nonnegative integer $k$ when $A, B$ are positive semi-definite), \[ \mathrm{tr}\bigl((A + B)^k\bigr) \le \sum_{\ell=0}^k \binom{k}{\ell} \mathrm{tr}\bigl(A^\ell B^{k-\ell}\bigr). \] The above natural inequality implies the classical Golden--Thompson inequality $\mathrm{tr}(e^{A + B}) \le \mathrm{tr}(e^A e^B)$. It also proves an extension, which can be used to show other new inequalities as well as give short proofs of inequalities such as the Schatten-$p$ two-point inequality for $p \ge 3$ and Hanner's inequality for $p \ge 3$. The main proof was discovered by Gemini Carbon within an agentic system.
item.dc:creator: Ravi Kumar, Raghu Meka

item.title: Nested Spherical Designs of Optimal Order
item.description: arXiv:2611.33856v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Zheng and Zhuang [22] showed that a spherical $t_1$-design $Y$ with $|Y|=M\sim t_1^d$ points on the sphere $\mathbb{S}^d$ can be extended to a spherical $t$-design by adding points, with a total of order $t^{2d+1}$, and asked whether the optimal order $t^d$ is attainable. We keep their construction and improve the estimate of the pairing of the given points against polynomials of unit $L^1$-gradient norm. We prove that, if the given spherical $t_1$-design is upper regular at scale $t_1$ (in particular if it is well-separated; such a design exists by Bondarenko, Radchenko and Viazovska [6]), then for $d\ge2$, every $N\ge C(d,K)\,t^d$ suffices to admit a point set $X$ with $|X|=N$, for all $t_1<t$, such that the multiset union $X\uplus Y$ is a spherical $t$-design; in particular $|X\uplus Y|\le C(d,K)\,t^d$. The proof combines the design property, which removes the low frequencies exactly, with an $L^1$ Jackson-type estimate and a sampling inequality applied on dyadic frequency blocks. Upper regularity turns out to be automatic for nested spherical designs of optimal order; that is, every spherical $t_1$-design with $M\le C_M t_1^d$ points extends to a spherical $t$-design with $N+M\le C(d)\,C_M\,t^d$ (with $C_M\ge1$), uniformly in $t_1<t$, without any separation hypothesis. Some control of local multiplicity is necessary for an extension of optimal order. We also show that the estimate of the pairing functional cannot be improved within this method; that is, for every point set of at most $c\,t^d$ points it is at least of order $t^{d-1}$, and for upper regular designs it is of exactly this order. Finally, we treat finite chains of nested spherical designs, and on the circle we remove a logarithmic factor from the general estimate.
item.dc:creator: Ali Raza Jatoi, Xiaosheng Zhuang

item.title: The modulus of smoothness and \(\ell_p\)-generation
item.description: arXiv:2611.34164v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fabian, Godefroy, H\'ajek and Zizler [\emph{J. Funct. Anal.} \textbf{200} (2003), 301--323, Theorem~2] proved that at density \(\aleph_1\), generation by a space whose modulus of smoothness has power type \(p\), \(1<p\le 2\), is equivalent to \(\ell_p(\Gamma)\)-generation. We extend this equivalence to arbitrary density, with \(|\Gamma|=\dens X\), answering \mbox{Problem~291} of Guirao, Montesinos and Zizler [\emph{Open Problems in the Geometry and Analysis of Banach Spaces}, Springer, Cham (2016), p.~127]. The proof combines an upper \(\ell_p\)-estimate on successive projection differences with transfinite induction on density. We characterize generation by superreflexive spaces and by their \(\ell_2\)-sums, and obtain \(\ell_{\min\{r,2\}}\)-generation for closed subspaces of \(L^r(\mu)\), \(1<r<\infty\), including Hilbert generation for \(r\ge 2\).
item.dc:creator: Zhiyao Fang, Wenwen Zhang, Ying Xu, Qi Liu

item.title: Separable models of an NIP Banach space theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.33260v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $Y$ be the renorming of $\ell_2(\mathbb N)\oplus_2\ell_2(\mathbb N)$ with norm $(h^2+q^2)^{1/2}$, where $h$ is the Hilbert norm and $q(u,v)=\sup_{i<j}|u_i+v_j|$. We prove that the unstable theory $\operatorname{Th}(Y)$ is NIP in the pure Banach language. We recover the index order from the Banach norm and classify the continuum many separable models up to surjective linear isometry. The invariants are the order type of a countable model of $\operatorname{Th}(\mathbb N,<)$ and the dimension of a separable Hilbert summand. Every such pair occurs. We describe all elementary embeddings between these models. The bounded norm types over a separable model are separable in the uniform metric exactly when its index order contains no copy of $(\mathbb Q,<)$.
item.dc:creator: Karim Khanaki, Pedro Poitevin

item.title: On Grokking and the Dynamics of Generalization
item.description: arXiv:2611.33825v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend the signal-channel theory of grokking introduced by Litman and Guo by relating training dissipation and evaluation transfer to population risk. For preconditioned gradient flows with time-dependent kernels, we distinguish two sources of limited evaluation visibility, namely small cumulative dissipation and weak transfer. We obtain quantitative bounds for task visibility and establish their stability under signal filtering and changes of evaluation distribution. We describe how task directions enter the effective signal channel through spectral activation or transport. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the transferred signal to decrease squared population risk and derive classification error bounds under margin assumptions. These results yield sufficient conditions for the same training trajectory to generalize under one evaluation distribution while failing under another. We show that differences in spectral learning rates can produce arbitrarily long delays between low training loss and low population risk. By relating classification accuracy to the distribution of margin crossing times, we construct a family of gradient flows in which the generalization delay tends to infinity, while both the duration of the transition from zero to full accuracy and the corresponding variation of population risk tend to zero. These phenomena occur without feature evolution during training. Finally, we prove that the occurrence and timing of generalization cannot generally be inferred from training dynamics alone, but depend on the geometry of evaluation transfer and its relation to the target.
item.dc:creator: Malik Amir

item.title: Parallel sums of nilpotent elements: exact realization and structured eigenvalue splitting
item.description: arXiv:2611.33877v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that, over every infinite field and for $m\ge2$, the parallel sums $N(N+C)^{-1}C$ of nilpotent $m\times m$ inputs with invertible sum are exactly the matrices of nullity at least two. Every positive split of the target nullity between the input kernels is realizable. Over $\mathbb{C}$, we determine the paired derivative image and characterize universal full matrix cancellation at nonzero residues. For analytic input paths, nilpotence is required only at the base. An adjugate identity forces the last two characteristic coefficients to be $O(\varepsilon^2)$, yielding sharp bounds $O(|\varepsilon|^{2/3})$ at nonzero three-dimensional nilpotent residues and $O(|\varepsilon|^{1/(m-2)})$ at nilpotent residues for $m\ge4$. At every base with residue of type $[m-1,1]$, $m\ge4$, we prove a generic splitting law, also with fixed input sum. For $m\ge5$, it has $m-2$ roots on the scale $|\varepsilon|^{1/(m-2)}$ and two on the scale $|\varepsilon|^{1/2}$, separating the largest-root and spectral-gap scales. A separate sharpness family keeps both inputs nilpotent and two roots zero. At the nonzero nilpotent three-dimensional boundary, a finite coefficient criterion computes the splitting orders for each exceptional affine fixed-sum direction. For each such path, the punctured spectral gap is at least $c|\varepsilon|^3$ near zero for some $c>0$, and the exponent is optimal over this class. Over a nonzero unital ring with $2$ invertible, we construct two $3\times3$ matrix inputs, each of nilpotency index exactly three, with invertible sum. In the complex unital Banach case, the residue has spectrum ${0}\cup\tfrac12\sigma(Q)$ for every coefficient $Q$. With the common core allowed to vary, a complex matrix is a finite-Drazin Hua output if and only if its nullity is not one.
item.dc:creator: Yaashaa Golovanov

item.title: Weak monotonicity, Critical exponents, and Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequalities on weighted graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.34017v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study weak monotonicity of heat kernel and ball averaged functionals on weighted graphs, and the associated critical exponents. Under sub-Gaussian heat kernel estimates, weak Bakry-\'Emery estimates for the semigroup are proved, with explicit values of the H\"older regularity exponent in the strongly recurrent case. Applications of the theory include Gagliardo-Nirenberg, Sobolev, Nash and isoperimetric inequalities on strongly recurrent graphs and their products.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Alonso Ruiz, Fabrice Baudoin, Li Chen

item.title: Differentiation and Ordered Optimization in Banach Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2605.05397v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we will define generalized critical point, ordered extreme and order monotone property of single-valued mappings in partially ordered Banach spaces. In particular, we will find the explicit formulas of Gateaux and Frechet derivatives of some single-valued mappings on the Banach spaces lp, for and C[0, 1], such as polynomial type operators and trigonometric type operators. By these concepts, we will investigate the connection between generalized critical points and ordered extrema of single-valued mappings in partially ordered Banach spaces that extends the connection between critical points and extrema of real valued functions in calculus. We will prove that in partially ordered Banach spaces, the order monotone of single-valued mappings can be described by its Gateaux derivatives or Frechet derivatives.
item.dc:creator: Jinlu Li

item.title: Subspaces of $L^1$ spanned by the even and odd levels of the Haar system
item.description: arXiv:2609.16735v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the closed subspace of $L^1[0,1]$ spanned by the even (respectively, odd) levels of the Haar system is not isomorphic to $L^1[0,1]$. Moreover, the closed span of any infinite collection of Haar levels with infinite complement is isomorphic to that of the even levels.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Speckhofer

item.title: Reflexive and strictly convex Banach spaces without Property (H)
item.description: arXiv:2609.23996v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that Property $(H)$ fails for a broad class of reflexive strictly convex Banach spaces. More generally, the real Banach space \[ \Big(\bigoplus_{j=1}^{\infty} L^{p_j}(\Omega_j,\mu_j)\Big)_{\ell^s} \] does not have Property $(H)$ whenever $1\le s<\infty$, $1\le p_j<\infty$, $\sup_j p_j=+\infty$, and each $L^{p_j}(\Omega_j,\mu_j)$ is infinite-dimensional.
item.dc:creator: Chunliu Feng, Geng Tian

item.title: An $L^p$ Version of Raeburn's Symmetric Imprimitivity Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.36677v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $1\leq p<\infty$. We prove an $L^p$-operator analogue of Raeburn's symmetric imprimitivity theorem for countable discrete groups. Let $A$ be an $L^p$-operator algebra with a contractive two-sided approximate identity, admitting a nondegenerate isometric representation on a $\sigma$-finite $L^p$-space. Given commuting free and proper actions of groups $G$ and $H$ on a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff space $Z$, together with commuting isometric actions on $A$, we show that the two corresponding full crossed products, and likewise the two reduced crossed products, are Morita equivalent as Banach algebras. The proof is organized through the linking groupoid. Its main analytic ingredient is a coefficient-valued spatial matrix dilation; in the reduced case we prove that this dilation preserves regularity after a Borel reindexing of the opposite corner. A pairing-valued approximate identity yields fullness and nondegeneracy.
item.dc:creator: Yeong Chyuan Chung

item.title: Concave shifts and the complete Nevanlinna--Pick property
item.description: arXiv:2611.12778v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a non-zero reproducing kernel Hilbert space of holomorphic functions on the unit disc, and assume $\mathcal{H}$ is invariant under the forward and backward shifts. We show that if the forward shift on $\mathcal{H}$ is concave, then $\mathcal{H}$ is a complete Nevanlinna--Pick (CNP) space. This answers a question by Shimorin, and greatly extends his result that any space of Dirichlet type is CNP. As a byproduct of our investigation, we also show that if the forward shift on $\mathcal{H}$ is concave, then any multiplier of $\mathcal{H}$ is the SOT limit of its Ces\`aro means. As applications, we prove a commutant lifting theorem for concave cyclic analytic operators, and several results about shift-invariant subspaces in de~Branges--Rovnyak spaces.
item.dc:creator: Shuaibing Luo, Eskil Rydhe

item.title: Rademacher and Enflo types in Banach spaces: sharp comparison and orthogonality
item.dc:creator: Zhiyao Fang, Qi Liu

item.title: Needlepoints in Quasi-Normed Orlicz Spaces and a Question of Kalton and Peck
item.description: arXiv:2611.31890v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the approachable points and the needlepoints coincide in every quasi-normed Orlicz function space on the probability interval. Their common set is either $\{0\}$ or $E_\Phi$. The proof gives a characterization by finite probability laws and also applies to Orlicz function spaces with the modular topology, without assuming $\Delta_2$. We then construct a separable real quasi-Banach space whose approachable points form a line and whose only needlepoint is zero. Every compact convex subset of this space is relatively locally convex. The construction gives a negative answer to the question of Kalton and Peck for general quasi-Banach spaces.
item.dc:creator: Dong Ji, Yunan Cui

item.title: Ergodic theorems for set maps under weak forms of additivity
item.description: arXiv:2501.14581v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate various relaxations of additivity for set maps into Banach spaces in the context of representations of amenable groups. Specifically, we establish conditions under which asymptotically additive and almost additive set maps are equivalent. For Banach lattices, we further show that these notions are related to a third weak form of additivity adapted to the order structure of the space. By utilizing these equivalences and reducing non-additive settings to the additive one by finding suitable additive realizations, we derive new non-additive ergodic theorems for amenable group representations into Banach spaces and streamline proofs of existing results in certain cases.
item.dc:creator: Raimundo Brice\~no, Godofredo Iommi

item.title: Quantitative BMO-BLO Estimates for the Hardy-Littlewood Maximal Function
item.dc:creator: Alejandro Claros

item.title: A Coarse-Geometric Interpretation of Holt's One-End Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2607.25846v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Can a group be colored red and blue, with both color classes infinite, so that each right translation changes the color of only finitely many elements? For the group of finite subsets of the natural numbers, one can color a nonempty set by the parity of its largest element (and the empty set red). Holt proved that no such coloring exists in an uncountable locally finite group. For the finitary coarse structure, right almost invariant subsets are exactly the coarsely clopen sets; modulo finite changes, their characteristic functions give all the projections in the Higson corona algebra. We give a detailed, self-contained account of Holt's coset argument in Cornulier's formulation, without using group cohomology. The argument shows why the space of coarse ends is a singleton and the full Higson corona is connected. We then give a proof of Protasov's stronger conclusion for any uncountable abelian group---in particular, an uncountable direct sum of groups of order two---showing that the full Higson corona is a singleton.
item.dc:creator: Hussain AL-Rasheed

item.title: Continuity equation on metric spaces via measure-valued derivations and BV-Wasserstein curves
item.description: arXiv:2608.28586v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a notion of continuity equation on metric spaces that is capable of describing curves of probability measures which are absolutely continuous or, more generally, of bounded variation (BV) with respect to the 1-Wasserstein distance. This continuity equation is based on a notion of measure-valued derivations, whose basic theory is also developed in this paper. On $\mathbb{R}^n$, our formulation is consistent with the continuity equation with singular flux introduced by Almi--Rossi--Savar\'e (arXiv:2506.15333), including the corresponding notion of minimal solutions when the norm is strictly convex. In this work, we characterize BV-curves in the space of probability measures equipped with the (extended) 1-Wasserstein distance as those curves satisfying the continuity equation with a measure-valued derivation of finite mass. To this aim, we extend our previous work (Calc. Var. (2024) 63:16) on probabilistic representations on BV-curves and construct from them measure-valued derivations (resp. flux measures) on geodesic metric spaces (resp. on $\mathbb{R}^n$).
item.dc:creator: Ehsan Abedi, Zhenhao Li, Timo Schultz

item.title: Failure of noncommutative Rota's theorem with $L(\log L)^\alpha$ endpoint
item.description: arXiv:2610.31560v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For every $1\le\alpha<2$, we construct a factorizable Markov map $T$ on a hyperfinite finite von Neumann algebra and a positive element $x\in L(\log L)^\alpha$ for which the sequence $T^n(T^*)^n x$ does not converge bilaterally almost uniformly. In particular, this answers a question of Anantharaman-Delaroche \cite{AD2006} concerning the $L\log L$ endpoint.
item.dc:creator: Hiranmoy Ghorui, Suman Mondal, Samya Kumar Ray

item.title: Controlled Riemannian rigidity
item.description: arXiv:2611.10854v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a compact Lie group acting smoothly and freely on a compact connected manifold, we prove that the space of invariant Riemannian metrics whose symmetry group is precisely the group in question is open dense in that of all invariant metrics provided the orbit space is at least 2-dimensional. This strengthens the author's prior results to their optimal dimension bound and recovers Ebin's non-equivariant analogue to the effect that trivial-symmetry Riemannian metrics constitute an open dense set. In the process, the discussion also addresses a number of apparent gaps in said sources, pertaining to the rigidity results in question.
item.dc:creator: Alexandru Chirvasitu
